question.problem: A cook designs a menu for his restaurant from Thursday to Sunday. Each day, only one main dish will be served, and it will not be repeated on any other day. If the cook wants to choose from the $9$ most popular dishes, how many different menus can the cook design?
question.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ popular dishes to choose from, so $n=9.$ We want to select $4$ of those for the menu, one for each day (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and Sunday), so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =3\,024.\end{aligned}
$$
